exposure: Mode of birth (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Maternal history of previous neonatal death
cohort: The study included 127 term neonates diagnosed with intrauterine growth restriction, excluding those born to diabetic mothers, with chronic disorders, birth asphyxia, or meconium aspiration.
finding: Hypoglycemia was found to be common, occurring in 40.9% of neonates with intrauterine growth restriction during a five-hour observation period, with the lowest mean blood glucose levels observed at three and four hours after birth.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered via cesarean section had a significantly lower frequency of hypoglycemia compared to those delivered vaginally.
cross-section timing: Hourly intervals for five hours post-birth, starting at birth
